title: The Account app's Notifications entry 403s for every non-admin — no permission set grants sys_inbox_message
body:
Browser-measured during the #7331 verification run (showcase, console dist built at objectui pin `8aad9fd50b16`). Filed unassigned for triage; not fixed in that card's PR because the fix is a security-baseline decision, not a QA edit.

## What happens

Sign in as a plain member — a user holding only business positions (in the showcase run: `contributor` + `finance`, plus the implicit `org_member` / `everyone`) — and open the **Account** app. Its `Inbox` group has two entries: **Notifications** and **Approvals**. Approvals works (that is what #7213 delivered). Notifications renders the "You don't have access" empty state.

The server says why, verbatim from the console error:

```
[Security] Access denied: operation 'find' on object 'sys_inbox_message'
is not permitted for positions [org_member, contributor, finance, everyone]
```

Every inbox-related read the shell issues for this session comes back `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`:

- `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message?top=20&sort=-created_at&filter=[...user_id...]`
- `GET /api/v1/data/sys_notification_receipt?top=200&filter=[...user_id..., channel=inbox]`
- `GET /api/v1/data/sys_activity?top=20&sort=-timestamp`

## Why it is not just this environment

`sys_inbox_message` is granted by **no shipped permission set**. `member_default` — the additive `everyone` baseline in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` — grants the better-auth identity tables plus `sys_user_preference`, and nothing else. That narrowing was a deliberate maintainer ruling (#5491: "the platform baseline narrows to explicit-allow … Everything else is the application's to declare"), and this finding does not dispute it.

The mismatch is that a **platform** app declares a nav entry to a **platform** object that no baseline names. `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/account.app.ts` says in its own docblock:

> we expose the same `sys_*` identity objects here and rely on RLS to scope rows to the caller. Crucially this app declares **no** `requiredPermissions`, so every authenticated user can reach it

The app is reachable, as designed. The object behind one of its entries is not.

## Consequences measured

1. The Account app's own Notifications entry is a dead end for the audience the app exists for.
2. The bell popover's notification half is structurally **0** for any non-admin: the popover badge for the test persona read `2`, which was `0 notifications + 2 pending approvals`. Only the approvals half of the #7213 badge breakdown can ever be non-zero for a business user.
3. It compounds #7266: the bell's "View all notifications" routes a non-admin to `/apps/setup/sys_inbox_message?view=mine`, so the user hits *both* the wrong-app routing and this missing grant at once. Fixing #7266's routing alone would still land on "You don't have access".

## Dispositions (not decided here)

1. Add an explicit `sys_inbox_message` (+ `sys_notification_receipt`) read grant to `member_default`, narrowed by a `_self` RLS policy on `user_id`, mirroring how `sys_user_preference` is handled there today.
2. Have the account app (or the messaging plugin) contribute the grant, keeping the platform baseline untouched — closer to the #5491 "the application declares it" principle, with the account app as that application.
3. Serve the personal inbox from a dedicated authenticated route instead of the generic data API, the way pending approvals already are, so no object grant is involved.
4. Accept it and retire the Notifications nav entry for non-admins.

No option recommended — this is a security-baseline call and option 1 widens a set whose narrowing was itself a ruling.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-08-10 on `examples/app-showcase` at framework `88154bee1`, console dist stamp `8aad9fd50b16750aebdd294392ff79540f17cd32`, non-admin persona created at runtime via better-auth sign-up and granted `contributor` + `finance`. Screenshots of the Account app's Notifications empty state and of the bell popover breakdown were captured in the run.
